entries.note: Tool implementation lives in a replaceable process behind the stable facade. Resolve only a validated runtime descriptor for the original host, retain the original root and reject foreign sessions/desktops before each operation. Probe/update/status never launches a coding conversation. The existing eight-tool connector can remain running while an agent uses runtime/client.mjs with its original context.

anchor.snippet: const windowCapability = state => { if (state.capabilities.projectWindows !== 1) throw new Error('Project-window control needs the current runtime supervisor. Use the documented context-bound bootstrap.'); };

entries.note: New window and report tools retain the connector’s captured root. Opening a window attaches an existing root-bound agent; only the recorded origin/project pair can inspect its window or exchange reports. The origin can explicitly view its linked project inbox or attribute its own project-side observation without claiming another agent wrote it.

anchor.snippet: const scriptCapability = state => { if (state.capabilities.scriptActions !== 1) throw new Error('Update the workspace worker before opening script tabs.'); };

entries.note: Script execution is effectful and not idempotent; root-bound tools require an explicit script path, literal argv and a target desktop. View attachment failure returns a retained process identity. show_session attaches that process without another execution, and ordinary stop_session remains the explicit termination action.

preview_file runs the project's own declared executable, so it is open-world and not read-only even though it never writes. The route returns the whole sanitized tree; the tool slices dir/depth and pages files with offset/limit, then shrinks depth and limit until the serialized reply fits the 32,000-character budget, reporting truncated/nextOffset (review finding 5). Command metadata is made root-relative and the generic tool wrapper replaces the absolute root path in error text with <root>. Entry text is bounded like read_file; the hex window is dropped because agents get size and SHA-256 instead.

anchor.snippet: const dashboardCapability = state => { if (state.capabilities.dashboard !== 1) throw new Error('This retained service predates the project dashboard. Update the workspace layer first.'); };

entries.note: dashboard_actions is read-only (availability only); dashboard_capture is open-world because it runs a project executable and writes files. Script and log actions deliberately get no new tool: scripts go through open_script with the listed script/args/env, logs start from the desktop tab and are followed with show_session/session_output, so process creation stays on the existing audited paths.

anchor.snippet: const gameCapability = state => { if (state.capabilities.projectGame !== 1) throw new Error('This retained service predates per-project game declarations. Update the workspace layer first.'); };

entries.note: game_preflight and launch_game address only the games the bound project declares in .rengine/project.json; their descriptions name no game, and the connector never carries a built-in executable or data path. Both take an optional gameId and default to the first declared record, so a single-game project needs no argument while a multi-game one is addressed explicitly and an unknown id is answered with the declared ids. launch_game is open-world because it executes the project's own program; it returns the running session of that same game id when one exists, so agents inspect the returned id rather than assuming a fresh process, and two declared games of one project can be running at once. The removed nolf_preflight/launch_nolf have no alias: nothing had shipped them to a user. The two tools gate on two capabilities, because the workspace layer can deliver only one of them: game_preflight needs projectGame, which the replaceable worker advertises for the route it serves itself, while launch_game needs projectGameLaunch, which only a session host that answers from the declaration can offer — replacing that host requires quiescence, so the refusal names it instead of telling the agent to update the workspace layer again.

anchor.snippet: tool('devices', 'List the devices the project declares in .rengine/project.json (contract 4, devices): where each target runs, with reachability, when it was checked, the reasons an unreachable device gives, and the games and dashboard actions bound to it — each bound action with the availability the dashboard computed for it (its own requires/tools composed with the device’s reachability) and each bound game with the preflight the launch uses, so a caller reads what can be run where without a second listing. The implicit local device is always listed. Reachability comes from each record’s own declared probe — bounded and side-effect-light rather than read-only, since adb starts its own daemon when none is running — run only on this call, cached briefly, and bypassed by refresh. Reachable means the device answered, never that a target can be launched on it: rEngine does not launch on a remote device, and the project’s own script action owns that.', {

entries.note: The devices tool is readOnlyHint (it changes nothing in the project) but openWorldHint, because it reaches the network or a USB device. Its description deliberately does NOT claim read-only: adb get-state and adb devices start the adb server when no daemon is running, so a probe is bounded and side-effect-light, not free of side effects. It also states that reachable is not launchable — a green ssh probe still cannot create a GL context in a logon session with no window station — so an agent does not read a reachable device as permission to launch on it. It gates on projectDevices, which the replaceable workspace worker advertises (KI-043: a capability served only by the retained host cannot be delivered by a layered update). The description now also states what each bound target carries — an action's availability as the dashboard computed it, a game's preflight — because the Devices tab renders those as controls and an agent reading this tool should not need a second listing to learn what can be run where.

Two of the six extended tools cannot be gated where the others are. The runtime supervisor answers /api/update-workspace and /api/desktop-action itself and forwards everything else to the workspace worker, so update_workspace and reload_desktop never reach the worker's gate and read the ledger here instead, before the call. The capability half is separate and applies to all six: agentToken says the worker serves a ledger, so an identified agent against a worker that does not advertise it is refused naming the layer to update rather than calling a worker that would pass every request. An anonymous caller — probeTools, an older launch with no identity — is not an agent and is never gated at all, which is what keeps update_workspace able to prepare its own replacement.

Two things live in the per-launch context and they have opposite rules. The BINDING -- url, token, instance, rootId -- is taken once from the facade's snapshot (RENGINE_MCP_CONTEXT_SNAPSHOT) precisely so that editing the file cannot retarget a running CLI to another project (spec 065); do not make the binding follow the file. The IDENTITY is the conversation, and the conversation can legitimately change under a running CLI: report-session.mjs rewrites this file when Claude Code's SessionStart hook says the process moved to another session id. So the identity alone is re-read, once per tool call at the top of scopedState, and identityHeaders is a function rather than a frozen object -- a frozen object passes workspace_info and still puts the stale id on the wire, which is the ledger's whole input. A missing, torn or anonymous file leaves the identity as it was rather than dropping it.
